attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite-dimensional PSD calculus is clear; the missing Yang-Mills input is a controlled reflected Wilson boundary OPE giving H,G and an o(eta^2) remainder for the locked observable algebra.
steps: Start with regulated reflection positivity: each fixed collar gives N^{a,L,delta}>=0 for reflected Wilson test families.
Use the RG-to-OS convergence topology to pass fixed-collar positivity to the continuum collar matrix N_delta and then to the collar limit \widehat N_eta, assuming the trace limit is valid.
After additive contacts vanish, write the collar-limit matrix as \widehat N_eta=\widehat B_eta\circ q_eta, where q_eta is the intended same-theory OS matrix.
Normalize diagonals and impose the rank-one boundary expansion q_eta=J+eta H+eta^2G+o(eta^2).
Decompose C^m=span{e}\oplus1^perp. Since the e-block is m+O(eta)>0, q_eta>=0 is equivalent to positivity of its Schur complement on 1^perp.
Expanding the Schur complement gives S_eta=eta PHP+eta^2(PGP-(1/m)PHee^*HP)+o(eta^2).

Therefore PHP>=0 is necessary. On null directions of PHP the order-eta term vanishes, so the displayed C-form is the next necessary obstruction; if it is negative, q_eta has a negative vector for small eta.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: We have not proved that the RG topology supplies this second-order collar expansion, that Wilson hairpin families are dense for OS testing, or that no hidden boundary counterterm changes the same theory.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Wilson boundary tangent cone

assumptions: Fixed-collar cutoff removal is valid: every finite reflected Wilson matrix entry converges in the RG topology.
Additive boundary contacts have vanished by diagonal trace continuity and positivity, so the remaining defect is multiplicative.
All entries of \widehat B_eta are nonzero for small eta, so Hadamard division is defined.
The quotient q_eta=\widehat N_eta\oslash\widehat B_eta has a Hermitian second-order expansion uniform on the chosen finite Wilson family.
The finite family is realized inside the locked gauge-invariant algebra, not enlarged by boundary states.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive cutoff/collar Schwinger matrices N^{a,L,delta}_{ij}=S_{a,L}(Theta W_i^delta,W_j^delta) for locked gauge-invariant Wilson observables.
target object: continuum Schwinger functional S on the same Wilson/local observable algebra whose finite reflected matrices are OS-positive after collar removal.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, with convergence valid for each finite reflected matrix entry and for the collar trace asymptotics.

same-theory condition: plane-touching Wilson observables are obtained by the no-new-boundary-counterterm collar trace in the locked renormalized algebra; only prelocked diagonal congruences may be ignored.
J is the m by m all-ones matrix, e=m^{-1/2}(1,...,1), and P=I-ee^* projects onto 1^perp.
\widehat B is the normalized multiplicative boundary Gram/anomaly factor and \widehat N is the normalized positive collar-limit matrix.

equations.label: exact Schur-preimage condition
equations.latex: \widehat N_\eta=\widehat B_\eta\circ q_\eta,\qquad q_\eta=\widehat N_\eta\oslash\widehat B_\eta,\qquad q_\eta\ge 0
equations.valid_when: The boundary defect is purely multiplicative and the intended same-theory OS matrix is obtained by dividing out that defect entrywise.

equations.label: rank-one expansion
equations.valid_when: The Wilson collar family approaches a common reflection-plane observable and the boundary OPE has a second-order finite-matrix asymptotic.

equations.label: Schur complement at J
equations.valid_when: Block-decompose q_eta relative to span{e}\oplus 1^perp; the e-block stays positive, equal to m+O(eta).

equations.label: first and second tangent gates
equations.valid_when: q_eta is positive semidefinite for all sufficiently small eta>0.

equations.label: second-order falsifier
equations.latex: u\in 1^\perp,\quad u^*PHPu=0,\quad u^*Cu<0\ \Longrightarrow\ q_\eta\not\ge0\text{ for small }\eta
equations.valid_when: C=PGP-(1/m)PHee^*HP and the remainder is o(eta^2) on the finite block.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute H and G from the reflected Wilson boundary OPE; a zero-sum vector in ker(PHP) with negative C-form is a concrete same-theory falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This bridge lemma converts Wilson boundary collar collapse from vague anomaly language into the tangent cone of the PSD cone at J, giving an explicit hierarchy of finite OS tests.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite locked Wilson collar family whose same-theory normalized OS matrix is q_eta=\widehat N_eta\oslash\widehat B_eta and q_eta=J+eta H+eta^2G+o(eta^2) near the rank-one matrix J, OS positivity forces PHP>=0 on 1^perp. If PHP has null space K, the next valid obstruction is C|_K>=0 with C=PGP-(1/m)PHee^*HP. A vector u in K with u^*Cu<0 is a finite same-theory falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the Wilson boundary OPE produces u^*Cu<0 for a realized locked family or if the topology cannot make the second-order expansion valid.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if reflected Wilson OPE estimates prove PHP>=0 and C>=0 on ker(PHP), with controlled higher-order remainder, on a dense locked Wilson core.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a concrete bridge lemma and a new finite obstruction hierarchy; the remaining work is analytic, not terminological.

dependency_updates.description: Fixed-collar closed-cone transfer remains valid, but the collar-collapse part now requires second-order tangent-cone control of reflected Wilson quotient matrices.
The locked algebra must realize the finite Wilson families and zero-sum tangent vectors used in the H and C tests.
Topology must control not only matrix entries but boundary OPE coefficients through o(eta^2) on finite OS blocks.
Need compute H and G for reflected hairpin/cusp collars and test PHP and the Schur-complement C on ker(PHP).

falsifiers: falsifier: a realized Wilson triple or quadruple with PHP>=0 but a vector u in ker(PHP) satisfying u^*Cu<0.
falsifier: failure of nonzero entrywise boundary factors, making q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B ill-defined for the intended Wilson block.
falsifier: a surviving additive contact with zero diagonal, contradicting the positive-contact vanishing argument and invalidating the multiplicative reduction.
falsifier: the cutoff-removal topology gives fixed-collar convergence but no valid second-order reflected collar expansion.
falsifier: the needed null vector exists only after enlarging the Wilson algebra by boundary states, so the calculation is not same-theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 217 identifies the next valid obstruction after the first-order kernel test. Near the rank-one quotient J, OS positivity is governed by the PSD tangent cone: first PHP>=0 on 1^perp, then a Schur-complement second-order form on ker(PHP). This is sharper than saying nonrank-one anomaly; it gives a computable finite falsifier from Wilson boundary OPE data.
